DAMGHANI:v1p468/r21.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r21.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r21.claim: Hajara can mean separation or withdrawal: avoid them graciously, or leave someone and not speak to him.
DAMGHANI:v1p468/r21.anchor: الثاني الهجر الانفراد والعزلة قوله تعالى في سورة المزمل واهجرهم هجرا جميلا أي اعتزلهم كقوله تعالى في سورة مريم واهجرني مليا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r4.claim: The father asks in a rebuking, denying tone whether Abraham is turning away from his idols; “desire away from” means deliberate rejection. He calls him by name, not “my son,” and speaks harshly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r4.anchor: استفهم استفهام إنكار، والرغبة عن الشيء تركه عمدا وآلهته أصنامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the predicate comes before the subject in arāghib anta because it matters most to the father and conveys astonishment that anyone would abandon the idols; this consoles Muhammad about similar treatment by Quraysh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r5.anchor: وقدم الخبر على المبتدأ في قوله أراغب أنت عن آلهتي لأنه كان أهم عنده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r6.claim: The author instead parses rāghib as the subject, licensed by the interrogative, and anta as the agent filling the predicate slot; this avoids inversion and avoids separating rāghib from its complement with an unrelated word.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p269/r6.anchor: والمختار في إعراب أراغب أنت أن يكون راغب مبتدأ لأنه قد اعتمد على أداة الاستفهام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r1.claim: The object of “stop” is omitted: the father may mean stop speaking to me this way and inviting me, or stop abandoning my idols; the threat answers an omitted oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r1.anchor: ومتعلق تنته محذوف واحتمل أن يكون عن مخاطبتي بما خاطبتني به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r2.speaker: الحسن، السدي، الضحاك، ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r2.claim: They interpret lan arjumannaka as stoning, killing, or insulting, respectively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: بالحجارة. وقيل: لأقتلنك. وقال السدي والضحاك وابن جريج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r3.speaker: الزمخشري، author، سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies an omitted “beware of me” before “leave me” to make the coordination parallel; the author says no deletion is needed because Sibawayh permits a declarative and imperative clause to be coordinated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r3.anchor: وإنما احتاج إلى حذف ليناسب بين جملتي العطف والمعطوف عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r4.speaker: الجمهور، الحسن، مجاهد، ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r4.claim: Most readers and these authorities take miliyyan as an adverb meaning a long time; its cognates refer to night and day or a lengthy period, and a poet uses it for an extended stretch of youth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r4.anchor: وانتصب مليا على الظرف أي دهرا طويلا قاله الجمهور والحسن ومجاهد وغيرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r5.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r5.claim: Sibawayh explains “walked upon him miliyyan” as meaning he stayed or traveled with him for a long time.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r6.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas and others gloss miliyyan as being safe and sound, a circumstantial description of the person addressed; Ibn Atiyya paraphrases it as being self-sufficient and independent of the father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r6.anchor: مليا معناه سالما سويا فهو حال من فاعل واهجرني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r7.speaker: السدي، ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says miliyyan means forever; Ibn Jubayr says a long time. The word's root conveys staying, as in tamallaytu ḥīnan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: معناه أبدا. ومنه قول مهلهل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers another sense: leave me while still able to go, before I beat and disable you; maliyy means physically capable and strong enough for something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p270/r8.anchor: أو مليا بالذهاب عني والهجران قبل أن أثخنك بالضرب

TABATABAI:6:74-83#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#5/r2.claim: The Qur’an presents Abraham first opposing the man it calls his father Azar over idols, insisting on monotheism until Azar expelled him and ordered him away.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#5/r2.anchor: بدأ بشأن رجل يذكر القرآن أنه كان أباه آزر، وقد أصر عليه أن يرفض الأصنام ويتبعه في دين التوحيد

BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r1.claim: The father answers stubbornly; the fronted question expresses astonishment that Abraham would turn from the idols, as though such rejection were irrational.
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r1.anchor: أمعرض ومنصرف أنت عنها بتوجيه الإنكار إلى نفس الرغبة

BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r2.claim: The threat is to stone Abraham to death or drive him away; another view takes stoning figuratively as verbal abuse and cursing.
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r2.anchor: يعني : الشتم والذم ومنه الرجيم المرمي باللعن

BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r3.claim: The command to leave means keep away for a long time, remain safe from the father, and stop speaking to him.
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r3.anchor: زمانا طويلا سالما مني ولا تكلمني من الملاوة وهو الدهر

BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r4.claim: R-j-m originally means throwing stones, from rijām, stones used for pelting.
BURSEVI:v5p258#3/r4.anchor: أصل الرجم الرمي بالرجام بالكسر وهي الحجارة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r1.claim: The father's reply is introduced as an answer to an implied question and shows him persisting in defiance, meeting Abraham's gentle advice with harshness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r1.anchor: استئناف مبنى على سؤال نشأ من صدر الكلام كأنه قيل فماذا قال ابوه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses “rاغب” as a fronted predicate and “you” as subject; fronting directs the rebuke at the very fact of turning away and adds astonishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r2.anchor: مبتدأ وفيه توجيه الأنكار إلى نفس الرغبه مع ضرب من التعجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء وابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa, Ibn Malik, and others parse “you” as the subject of the participle, licensed by the preceding interrogative, avoiding separation of “rاغب” from its complement.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r3.anchor: فاعل الصفة لتقدم الاستفهام وهو مغن عن الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r4.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r4.claim: Al-Kashf answers that the subject is not wholly foreign, since the separated phrase is a prepositional phrase understood later; the word order is rhetorically viable and heightens denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r4.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشف : المبتدأ ليس اجنبيا من كل وجه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers the Abu al-Baqa analysis because it avoids separation and an unusual fronting; the author also reports the rival rhetorical case for fronting as stronger in denunciation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r5.anchor: ورجح أو حيان اعراب أبى البقاء ومن معه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r6.speaker: البدر الدماميني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r6.claim: Al-Badr al-Damamini hesitates to treat the delayed noun as subject in patterns like “Is the sun rising?”, fearing confusion with an object/agent construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r6.anchor: وتوقف البدر الدماميني في جواز ابتدائية المؤخر في مثل هذا التركيب وان خلا عن فصل أو محذور آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r7.speaker: الشمني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r7.claim: Al-Shumni replies that the first construction has two possible readings, both marked, creating ambiguity rather than the role confusion found in “Zayd struck.”
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r7.anchor: واجاب الشمنى بأن زيدا في الأول يحتمل أمرين كل منهما بخلاف الأصل وذلك اجمال لا لبس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r8.claim: The threat means that if Abraham does not stop rebuking idolatry and calling his father to his message, his father will stone him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r8.anchor: أي والله لئن لم تنته عما انت عليه من النهي عن عبادتها والدعوة إلى ما دعوتني اليه لأرجمنك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r9.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r9.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the threatened stoning literally as throwing stones.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r9.anchor: لأرجمنك بالحجارة على ما روى عن الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والضحاك وابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Jurayj report a figurative threat to revile or insult Abraham with the tongue.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r10.anchor: باللسان والمراد لاشتمنك وروى ذلك عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r11.claim: A few construe the command as telling Abraham to stop turning away from the idols, but al-Alusi says that interpretation is not sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r11.anchor: وقدر بعضهم متعلق النهي الرغبه عن الآلهه أي لئن لم تنته عن الرغبه عن آلهتي لأرجمنك وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies an omitted command, “beware me,” before “leave me,” avoiding a mismatch between the threat and an imperative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r12.anchor: أي فاحذرني واتركني والى ذلك ذهب الزمخشري

ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r13.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r13.claim: Others coordinate “leave me” with the preceding sentence, invoking Sibawayh's allowance for coordination between clauses of different kinds; the author notes that this ordering is more affecting.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p98/r13.anchor: ومن الناس من عطف على الجملة السابقة بناء على تجويز سيبويه العطف مع التخالف في الأخبار والإنشاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r1.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and a group interpret “for a long while” as a long duration.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r1.anchor: أي دهرا طويلا عن الحسن ومجاهد وجماعه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r2.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r2.claim: Al-Suddi glosses the command as “begin” or “go ahead,” which al-Alusi regards as the likely contextual sense; the underlying word is linked to extension over time.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r2.anchor: السدى : ابدأ وكأنه المراد واصله على ما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r3.claim: The form is used adverbially for a long time, as in the line of Muhalhil describing mountains splitting and widows mourning for a long while.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r3.anchor: فتصدعت صمم الجبال لموته وبكت عليه المرملات مليا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r4.claim: One report from Ibn Abbas glosses the word as “long,” without naming the thing whose duration is meant, allowing a source or adverbial analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن الأنباري عن ابن عباس أنه فسره بطويلا ولم يذكر الموصوف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r5.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas reads it as safe, sound, and able to leave before being beaten into helplessness; on this reading it describes Abraham's condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p99/r5.anchor: وفي روايه أخرى عن ابن عباس أن المعنى سالما سويا والمراد قادرا على الهجر مطيقا له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r6.claim: Abraham's father asks whether Abraham is turning away from his idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r6.anchor: {قال} أبوه مجيبا له: {أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r7.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r7.claim: They interpret the threat to stone Abraham as insulting him with vile speech and driving him away through abusive words.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r7.anchor: الكلبي ومقاتل والضحاك: لأشتمنك ولأبعدنك عني بالقول القبيح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the threat as beating Abraham.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r9.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234/r9.claim: ʿIkrima interprets the threat as killing Abraham with stones.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says “for a long while” means stay far away from me for a long time.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r2.claim: Mujahid and ʿIkrima take the phrase to mean for a time.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says it means for an age; the root sense of ḥīn is remaining.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r3.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: دهرا وأصل "الحين": المكث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r4.claim: The dual al-malawān is a name for night and day.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r5.speaker: قتادة وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r5.claim: Qatada and Ata explain the phrase as “safely.”

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham is to leave safely, without his father inflicting harm; a person “mali” in a matter is capable of it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p234#2/r6.anchor: ابن عباس: اعتزلني سالما لا تصيبك مني معرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r1.claim: The father answers tenderness with harshness, calls Abraham by name rather than “my son,” and uses an interrogative to express astonished rejection; the threat may mean insult, stoning, or expulsion.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r1.anchor: قابل استعطافه ولطفه في الارشاد بالفظاظة وغلظة العناد

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r2.claim: “A long while” can mean a long time or going far away.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:46-47/r2.anchor: زمانا طويلا من الملاوة أو مليا بالذهاب عني

BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r5.claim: The father's reply contrasts harsh ignorance with Abraham's refined manners and sound wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r5.anchor: مقابلا لذلك الأدب العظيم والحكمة البالغة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r6.claim: Fronting the predicate in arāghib conveys surprise and rejection; direct address and “my gods” stress confrontation and his own exaggerated reverence for idols.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r7.claim: Calling Abraham by name instead of a kinship title signals rupture; the oath threatens to stone or kill him unless he stops, then commands a long separation.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r8.claim: Abraham's mistreatment consoles the Prophet for abuse by Quraysh and his uncle Abū Lahab.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p537/r8.anchor: تسلية لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم وتأسية

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r4.claim: He glosses Abraham's threat to stone his father as a threat to insult him.
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {لأرجمنك} قال: لأشتمنك

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r5.claim: He explains Abraham's command to be left for a long while as telling his father to avoid him safely before punishment might reach him.
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {واهجرني مليا} قال: اجتنبني سالما قبل أن يصيبك مني عقوبة

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r6.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r6.claim: Ikrima gives the same gloss of being left safely.

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r7.claim: He glosses the request for a long separation as leaving while safe.
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {واهجرني مليا} قال: سالما

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r8.claim: Al-Hasan gives the same gloss: safely.

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r9.claim: He interprets the separation as lasting for a time.

DURR-FULL:v5p512/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r10.claim: He glosses مليا as a long time and cites al-Muhalhil's line, where مليا describes the duration of mourning.
DURR-FULL:v5p512/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله: {واهجرني مليا} ما الملي قال: طويلا

QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r7.claim: Abraham's father threatened him after Abraham offered a gracious promise of good; Abraham answered from settled insight while still retaining hope.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r2.claim: Abraham repeats “O father” four times to persuade gently; this expansive setting contrasts with Noah’s single address to his son in a concise setting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p114/r2.anchor: أربع مرات تكرير اقتضاه مقام استنزاله إلى قبول الموعظة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r6.claim: The clause “he said” explicitly separates the dialogue, as in another Qur’anic dialogue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r6.anchor: لوقوعها في المحاورة كما تقدم في قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r7.claim: The father’s question indignantly rejects Abraham’s departure from idol worship; possessively attaching the idols to himself asserts his authority and honors himself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r7.anchor: إضافة الآلهة إلى ضمير نفسه إضافة ولاية وانتساب إلى المضاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r8.claim: The father answers with rudeness and arrogance, unlike Abraham’s gentleness, revealing hardness of heart and entrenched disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p117/r8.anchor: وقد جاء في جوابه دعوة ابنه بمنتهى الجفاء والعنجهية بعكس ما في كلام إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r1.claim: The command to leave coordinates with the threat: stoning is a deferred penalty, while exclusion from company and conversation is immediate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r1.anchor: وجملة واهجرني مليا عطف على جملة لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r2.claim: Hajr means cutting conversation and companionship; ordering his son to leave rather than announcing his own departure casts it as expulsion and humiliation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r2.anchor: قطع المكالمة وقطع المعاشرة ، وإنما أمر أبو إبراهيم ابنه بهجرانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r3.claim: Maliyyan means a long time, with no known simple verb or verbal noun; it derives from a disused source and modifies an omitted cognate object, “a long abandonment.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r3.anchor: ومليا : طويلا ، وهو فعيل ، ولا يعرف له فعل مجرد ولا مصدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r4.claim: Alternatively, maliyyan modifies an omitted time noun, since al-malā often means a period; the explanation compares this ellipsis with the expression “a ship with planks.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p120/r4.anchor: بناء على أن الملا مقصورا غالب في الزمان فذكره يغني عن ذكر موصوفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r10.claim: Āzar, identified here as Tarikh, asks whether Abraham is turning away; desire can be for something or away from it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r10.anchor: قال آزر وهو تارخ أراغب أنت عن آلهتي، والرغبة ميل النفس، فقد تكون الرغبة في الشيء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r11.claim: The preferred syntax makes rāghib the subject and anta the agent filling its predicate slot; a fronted predicate is also possible, but Sibawayh's first parse is better.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r11.anchor: وقوله أراغب رفع بالابتداء وأنت فاعل به يسد مسد الخبر وحسن ذلك وقربه اعتماد «راغب» على ألف الاستفهام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r12.claim: Abraham's father carved and sold idols and urged people to worship them, so he rebuked Abraham's refusal and threatened him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r12.anchor: وكان فيما روي ينحتها وينجرها بيده ويبيعها ويحض عليها فقرر ابنه إبراهيم على رغبته عنها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r13.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r13.claim: Al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Dahhak take “I will stone you” figuratively as “I will insult you.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r13.anchor: فقال السدي وابن جريج والضحاك: معناه بالقول، أي لأشتمنك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r14.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r14.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the threat literally as stoning with rocks; another faction understands it as killing him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r14.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: معناه لأرجمنك بالحجارة، وقالت فرقة: معناه لأقتلنك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r15.claim: On the literal killing interpretations, “leave me” is a separate order because Abraham cannot depart after being stoned; on the insult reading, it means leave for a while or safely.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r15.anchor: وقوله واهجرني على هذا التأويل إنما يترتب بأنه أمر على حياله كأنه قال: إن لم تنته لأقتلنك بالرجم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r16.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r16.claim: Maliyyan means a long time, from the night and day periods; Ibn Abbas and others instead take it as safe and sound, a circumstantial description of Abraham.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r16.anchor: ومليا معناه دهرا طويلا مأخوذ من الملوين وهما الليل والنهار وهذا قول الجمهور والحسن ومجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas and others gloss maliyyan as untroubled and self-sufficient, describing Abraham's state.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p18/r17.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره مليا معناه سليما منا سويا فهو حال من إبراهيم عليه السلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r1.claim: Abraham's father says he will stone him if he does not stop criticizing and insulting the idols.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r1.anchor: أتارك عبادتها انت لئن لم تنته عن عيبها وشتمها لأرجمنك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r2.claim: One interpretation of la-arjumannaka is verbal abuse and cursing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r2.anchor: أحدهما بالشتم والقول قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r3.claim: Another interpretation is actual stoning, forcing Abraham to distance himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r3.anchor: والثاني بالحجارة حتى تتباعد عني قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r4.speaker: ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r4.claim: One view takes maliyyan as a long time, also held by Hasan, al-Farrāʾ, and most authorities; Ibn Qutayba glosses it as a long period.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r4.anchor: اهجرني طويلا رواه ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس وبه قال الحسن والفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r5.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r5.claim: Another view says leave me safely before my punishment strikes; Qatada and al-Ḍaḥḥāk agree, explaining the word as having strength and capacity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r5.anchor: أجتنبني سالما قبل أن تصيبك عقوبتي رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r6.claim: On the second reading, Abraham is told to leave while keeping his dignity and remaining safe from harm.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p237/r6.anchor: فالمعنى اهجرني وعرضك وافر وأنت سليم من أذاي

SULAMI:v1p427#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p427#3/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p427#3/r1.claim: After his father spoke ignorantly, invited him to idols, and threatened him, Abraham answered with a peaceful greeting, like the response to ignorant people in 25:63.
SULAMI:v1p427#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : لما بدا منه كلام الجهال من الدعوة إلى آلهته والوعيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r1.claim: Abraham's father means that if he will not worship the idols he must stop insulting them; otherwise he threatens retaliation and abuse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r1.anchor: فانته عن سبها وشتمها وعيبها، فإنك إن لم تنته عن ذلك اقتصصت منك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، ابن جريج، الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r2.claim: These authorities explain the father's threat as threatening to stone or revile Abraham.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r2.anchor: وهو (5) قوله: {لأرجمنك} ، قاله ابن عباس، والسدي، وابن جريج

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r3.claim: They interpret the command to leave for a while as a long time.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن إسحاق: يعني دهرا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan also interprets the requested separation as a long time.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the father meant Abraham should leave forever.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatada, Atiyya, and Abu Malik say leave safely before punishment; Ibn Jarir chooses this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p235#2/r6.anchor: سويا سالما، قبل أن تصيبك مني عقوبة. وكذا قال الضحاك، وقتادة وعطية الجدلي

JISHUMI:v6p4566/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r6.claim: Raghba in something is desire to obtain it for benefit; raghba away from it is turning aside from harm. It can also mean abundant giving.
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r6.anchor: الرغبة في الشيء نقيض الرغبة عنه

JISHUMI:v6p4566/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r7.claim: Intihāʾ means refraining from a forbidden act; its root concerns reaching a limit.
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r7.anchor: والانتهاء: الامتناع من الفعل المنهي عنه

JISHUMI:v6p4566/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r8.claim: Rajm means stoning or insult; its root is stones.

JISHUMI:v6p4566/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r9.claim: Maly means a span of time; the dual may denote night and day, and respite prolongs someone's days.
JISHUMI:v6p4566/r9.anchor: مليا: حينا ومدة، يقال: أقام ملاوة من دهر

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r12.claim: Threats instead of answering Abraham's argument illustrate the helplessness of falsehood that abandons proof.
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r12.anchor: على عجزه عن جواب الحجة، وهكذا طريقة كل مبطل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r1.claim: After Abraham's proofs and tactful counsel, his father answers with harsh disbelief, calls him by name, and does not reciprocate yā-abati with a tender 'my son'.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r1.anchor: أقبل عليه الشيخ بفظاظة الكفر وغلظة العناد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r2.claim: In arāghib anta, the predicate precedes the subject because the question of abandoning the idols is foremost to the father; the order conveys surprise and rejection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r2.anchor: وقدم الخبر على المبتدأ في قوله : { أراغب أنت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r3.claim: This exchange comforts the Prophet regarding similar treatment from his own people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r3.anchor: وفي هذا سلوان وثلج لصدر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r4.claim: La-arjumannaka may mean I will insult you with my tongue, as a rajīm is one cast out by cursing.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, it threatens to kill him by stoning or drive him away by throwing stones; rajm fundamentally means throwing stones.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r5.anchor: أو لأقتلنك ، من رجم الزاني . أو لأطردنك رميا بالحجارة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r6.claim: Maliyyan can mean for a long time, from malāh, or a long-lasting departure before the father beats him so he cannot leave; the phrase can mean able to endure something.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r6.anchor: زمانا طويلا من الملاوة : أو مليا بالذهاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p22#2/r7.claim: Wa-hjurnī coordinates with an omitted 'beware of me,' implied by the threat la-arjumannaka.

FARRA:v2p169/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p169/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p169/r1.claim: La-arjumannaka means ‘I will insult or revile you.’

FARRA:v2p169/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p169/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p169/r2.claim: Maliyyan means a long time; several dialect forms—malwah and malāwah—share the sense of duration.
FARRA:v2p169/r2.anchor: وقوله: (واهجرني مليا) طويلا يقال كنت عنده ملوة من دهر وملوة وملوة وملاوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r1.claim: The threat to stone Abraham means throwing stones until he goes away.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r1.anchor: بالحجارة حتى تباعد عني , قاله الحسن . الثاني : لأرجمنك بالذم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r2.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r2.claim: It may instead mean reviling and defaming him verbally; al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj share this view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r2.anchor: بالذم باللسان والعيب بالقول , قاله الضحاك , والسدي , وابن جريج

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r3.claim: Maliyyan can mean a long time; Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, and al-Suddi agree, and Muhalhil's verse uses the word in mourning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r3.anchor: دهرا طويلا , قاله الحسن , ومجاهد , وابن جبير , والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r4.claim: Maliyyan may mean safe and sound, free of punishment; Qatada, al-Dahhak, and ʿAtaʾ share this view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r4.anchor: سويا سليما من عقوبتي , قاله ابن عباس , وقتادة , والضحاك , وعطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r5.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r5.claim: Maliyyan may mean for a time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p374/r5.anchor: الثالث : حينا ، قاله عكرمة . قوله تعالى : { قال سلام عليك

MUJAHID:v1p386#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p386#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p386#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the command to leave Abraham alone for maliyyan as for a time.
MUJAHID:v1p386#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ واهجرني مليا ﴾ قال حينا

MUQATIL:19:45-48/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r2.claim: Azar asks whether Ibrahim rejects his idols and threatens to stone him, meaning insult him here; elsewhere in the Qur'an the same threat means killing.
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r2.anchor: يعني لئن لم تسكت لأشتمنك، { واهجرني مليا } [آية: 46]

MUQATIL:19:45-48/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r3.claim: Maliyyan means for the length of Azar's life or, alternatively, for a long time: Ibrahim must leave and prolong the separation.
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r3.anchor: يعني أيام حياتك، ويقال: طويلا، واعتزلني وأطل هجراني

MUQATIL:19:45-48/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains Azar's instruction as leaving him unharmed, without suffering injury from him.
MUQATIL:19:45-48/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: واعتزلنى سالم العرض لا يصيبك منى معرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r1.claim: Azar rebukes Abraham, uses his name rather than يا أبت, and puts the predicate before the subject because the question of rejecting the idols matters most.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r1.anchor: آزر توبيخا ﴿ أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم ﴾ أي اترغب عن عبادتها فناداه باسمه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r2.claim: The threat is to stop Abraham insulting the idols; لأرجمنك may mean kill by stones, drive him away by throwing stones, or revile him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r2.anchor: عن شتم الأصنام ﴿ لأرجمنك ﴾ لأقتلنك بالرجام أولأضربنك بها حتى تتباعد أو لآشتمنك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r3.claim: The command to leave is coordinated with an implied warning: fear me and leave me.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r3.anchor: عطف على محذوف يدل عليه لارجمنك تقديره فاحذرنى واهجرنى

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r4.claim: مليا is a temporal adverb meaning for a long time, derived from a word for an extended period.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39/r4.anchor: ظرف أي زمانا طويلا من الملاوة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r1.claim: La-arjumannaki means I will revile or insult you.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r2.claim: Maliyyan means for a long while; tamallaytu ḥabībaka means spending a long time with your beloved.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r2.anchor: {واهجرني مليا} أي حينا طويلا (1) . ومنه يقال: تمليت حبيبك.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p274#5/r3.claim: Al-malawān are the night and day.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r9.claim: Abraham’s father asks whether he is turning away from his gods.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r10.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r10.claim: Hasan says Abraham’s father threatened to stone him.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r10.anchor: قال الحسن: يعني بالحجارة. الضحاك: بالقول أي لأشتمنك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r11.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak says the threat means he would verbally abuse Abraham.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r11.anchor: الضحاك: بالقول أي لأشتمنك. ابن عباس: لأضربنك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas says the threat means he would beat Abraham.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r12.anchor: ابن عباس: لأضربنك. وقيل: لأظهرن أمرك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r13.claim: Another interpretation of the threat is that he would expose or publicize Abraham’s affair.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets leave me for a long while as withdrawing safely, without harm from his father; al-Tabari prefers this, and Qurtubi notes that it makes the word circumstantial for Abraham.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r14.anchor: أي اعتزلني سالم العرض لا يصيبنك مني معرة واختاره الطبري

QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r15.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:19:41-46/r15.claim: Hasan and Mujahid interpret the phrase as leave me for a long period, deriving it from a word for a stretch of time.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r1.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r1.claim: Al-Kisa’i records several forms meaning a long span of time; on that interpretation the word functions adverbially.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47/r1.anchor: قال الكسائي: يقال هجرته مليا وملوة وملوة وملاوة وملاوة

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r1.claim: Abraham answered his father’s idolatry with monotheistic proof and gentle exhortation, while his father answered with imitation, insult, and threat; God recounts this to comfort Muhammad amid polytheist abuse.
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما دعا أباه

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r2.claim: If the father’s question is genuine, it is futile because he already knew from repeated admonition that Abraham rejected the idols.
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r2.anchor: فإن كان ذلك على وجه الاستفهام فهو خذلان لأنه قد عرف منه ما تكرر منه من وعظه وتنبيهه

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r3.claim: If the father speaks in amazement, the real cause for amazement is rational people worshipping idols, not rejecting an argument that disproves them.
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r3.anchor: وإن كان ذلك على سبيل التعجب فأي تعجب

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r4.claim: The father’s baseless astonishment countered Abraham’s reasoned astonishment that an intelligent person would worship idols.
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r4.anchor: ذلك التعجب الظاهر المبني على الدليل

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says rajm throughout the Qur’an means verbal abuse, insult, or blame.
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r5.anchor: الرجم في القرآن كله بمعنى الشتم

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes rajm literally as throwing stones by hand.

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r7.claim: One reported interpretation is that the father would expose Abraham to the people so they would stone and kill him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r7.anchor: لأرجمنك بإظهار أمرك للناس ليرجموك ويقتلوك

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that the father would stone Abraham to make him go far away.

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r9.speaker: المؤرج
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r9.claim: Al-Mu’arrij says rajm means “I will kill you” in Quraysh dialect.

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r10.claim: Abu Muslim reads rajm as stoning, extended figuratively to expulsion and distance; the following command to leave supports expulsion.
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو مسلم لأرجمنك المراد منه الرجم بالحجارة إلا أنه قد يقال ذلك في معنى الطرد والإبعاد

RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r11.claim: The basic sense of rajm is pelting with stones, so the literal sense is preferable; “leave me” does not prove verbal insult because it tells Abraham to flee the threat.
RAZI-FULL:v21p194#2/r11.anchor: واعلم أن أصل الرجم هو الرمي بالرجام فحمله عليه أولى

RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r1.claim: “Leave me” is interpreted either as ending speech or as physically leaving the house and country, as the Messenger and believers migrated.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r1.anchor: أحدهما : المراد واهجرني بالقول . والثاني : بالمفارقة في الدار والبلد وهي هجرة الرسول والمؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r2.claim: Physical separation from the father is closer to the apparent meaning of the command.

RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r3.claim: One reading of maliyyan means for a long time, from the expression for a long stretch of time.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r3.anchor: مليا أي مدة بعيدة مأخوذ من قولهم أتى على فلان ملاوة من الدهر

RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r4.claim: Another reading means leave while still able to go, before the father beats and incapacitates him; the word can mean capable and able.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195/r4.anchor: عني والهجران قبل أن أثخنك بالضرب حتى لا تقدر أن تبرح

RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r1.claim: The coordination “and leave me” omits an implied “beware me,” supplied by the threat of stoning: beware me and leave lest I stone you.
RAZI-FULL:v21p195#2/r1.anchor: عطف اهجرني على معطوف عليه محذوف يدل عليه لأرجمنك ، أي فاحذرني واهجرني

STUDYQURAN:19:46/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:46/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:46/r1.claim: The threat to stone Abraham generally means cursing or verbally attacking him; some commentators allow a literal threat of physical stoning.
STUDYQURAN:19:46/r1.anchor: threatening to curse him or to “stone him with words”

STUDYQURAN:19:46/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:46/r2.speaker: Quran commentators
STUDYQURAN:19:46/r2.claim: The order to leave for a long while likely tells Abraham to go so he will be safe from his father's punishment.
STUDYQURAN:19:46/r2.anchor: Take leave of me so that you will be safe from my punishment

NAHHAS:v3p18/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p18/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p18/r4.claim: In Abraham's question, أنت is the subject and fills the predicate slot after راغب; an indefinite subject is apt after the preceding phrase.
NAHHAS:v3p18/r4.anchor: رفع بالابتداء و أنت فاعل سد مسد الخبر كما تقول أقائم أنت

TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r1.claim: Abraham's father asks if he rejects worship of his idols and threatens him for speaking ill of them, telling him to stop.
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r1.anchor: آلهتي؟ {لئن} [المائدة: 12] أنت {لم تنته} [مريم: 46] عن ذكرها بسوء

TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī glosses the threat to stone Abraham as verbal abuse, insults, and foul speech.
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r2.anchor: عن السدي، {قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي، يا إبراهيم لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك} [مريم: 46] بالشتيمة والقول

TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r3.claim: He explains the threat as insulting speech.
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r3.anchor: عن السدي، {قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي، يا إبراهيم لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك} [مريم: 46] بالشتيمة والقول

TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r4.claim: He glosses it as threatening to insult Abraham verbally.
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r4.anchor: قال ابن جريج، في قوله: {لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك} [مريم: 46] قال: بالقول لأشتمنك

TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r5.claim: He calls the threat verbal stoning.
TAB-FULL:v15p551#3/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {لأرجمنك} [مريم: 46] يعني: رجم القول

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says interpreters differed: one view takes maliyyan as a lengthy period, deriving it from the word for a long span of time.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] قال: دهرا

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses maliyyan as an age or long time.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] قال: دهرا

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r3.claim: Mujāhid also glosses it as a period of time.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله {مليا} [مريم: 46] قال حينا

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it means a long time.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، عن الحسن، {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] قال: طويلا

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan also says it means a long period.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r5.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] قال: زمانا طويلا

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq glosses it as an age and connects the word to the meaning of an age.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r6.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] يقول: دهرا، والدهر: الملي

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses it as an age.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] قال دهرا

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r9.claim: A second interpretation takes maliyyan as leaving safely and soundly, without punishment.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r9.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: واهجرني سويا سالما من عقوبتي إياك،

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as leaving safely.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] يقول: اجتنبني سويا

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says to depart safely before his father harms or punishes him.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] قال: اجتنبني سالما قبل أن يصيبك مني عقوبة

TAB-FULL:v15p554/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r12.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r12.claim: Qatāda glosses maliyyan as leaving safely.
TAB-FULL:v15p554/r12.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] قال: سالما

TAB-FULL:v15p555/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r1.speaker: عطية الجدلي
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r1.claim: ʿAṭiyyah al-Jadalī glosses maliyyan as safely.
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r1.anchor: عن عطية الجدلي، {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] قال: سالما

TAB-FULL:v15p555/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says to keep away safely so no harm comes from the father.
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله {واهجرني مليا} [مريم: 46] اجتنبني سالما لا يصيبك مني معرة

TAB-FULL:v15p555/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the safe, unharmed interpretation because it follows the threat to stone Abraham: leave before punishment reaches him.
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r3.anchor: وأولى القولين بتأويل الآية عندي قول من قال: معنى ذلك: واهجرني سويا، سلما من عقوبتي،

TAB-FULL:v15p555/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r4.claim: He rejects the long-time interpretation because the preceding threat makes an order to leave safely apt, while nothing supports prolonged estrangement.
TAB-FULL:v15p555/r4.anchor: فأما الأمر بطول هجره فلا وجه له

TABATABAI:19:44-47/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r6.claim: The words describe rejection of Abraham’s religion, cessation after warning, stoning, and prolonged separation; stoning is the degrading killing of an outcast.
TABATABAI:19:44-47/r6.anchor: والانتهاء الكف عن الفعل بعد النهي، والرجم الرمي بالحجارة

TABRISI:19:41-44/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:41-44/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:41-44/r4.claim: Rajm means throwing stones or insulting; its root is connected with stones.
TABRISI:19:41-44/r4.anchor: والرجم الرمي بالحجارة والرجم الشتم وأصله من الرجم والرجام وهو الحجارة

TABRISI:19:41-44/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:41-44/r5.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:19:41-44/r5.claim: Maliyyan means a long time, and al-Farrāʾ lists several dialect forms.
TABRISI:19:41-44/r5.anchor: والملي الدهر الطويل قال الفراء يقال كنت عندنا ملوة وملوة

TABRISI:19:41-44/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:41-44/r8.speaker: الزجاج والخليل وسيبويه
TABRISI:19:41-44/r8.claim: Arabians say yā abat and yā umat; al-Khalīl and Sībawayh take tāʾ as a substitute for possessive yāʾ, like yā ʿamma.
TABRISI:19:41-44/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج العرب تقول في النداء يا أبت ويا أمت

TABRISI:19:41-44/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:41-44/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:41-44/r9.claim: Maliyyan is an adverbial accusative; kullan in the later passage is an object of jaʿalnā.
TABRISI:19:41-44/r9.anchor: وقوله مليا منصوب على الظرف وكلا مفعول جعلنا

TABRISI:19:45-48/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:45-48/r9.claim: Āzar asks whether Ibrahim has turned away from worshipping his idols.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r9.anchor: أي أمعرض أنت عن عبادة آلهتي التي هي الأصنام

TABRISI:19:45-48/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r10.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
TABRISI:19:45-48/r10.claim: One interpretation of the threat is that Āzar will stone Ibrahim.

TABRISI:19:45-48/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r11.speaker: السدي وابن جريج
TABRISI:19:45-48/r11.claim: Another interpretation is that Āzar will accuse and insult him.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r11.anchor: وقيل: لأرمينك بالذنب والعيب وأشتمنك عن السدي وابن جريج

TABRISI:19:45-48/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:45-48/r12.claim: A third interpretation takes the threat to mean that Āzar will kill Ibrahim.

TABRISI:19:45-48/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r13.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والسدي
TABRISI:19:45-48/r13.claim: Maliyyan can mean a long time, so Āzar orders Ibrahim to leave for an extended period.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r13.anchor: أي فارقني دهرا طويلا عن الحسن ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير والسدي

TABRISI:19:45-48/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:45-48/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وعطاء والضحاك
TABRISI:19:45-48/r14.claim: Alternatively, maliyyan means sound and secure from punishment, fully capable in an affair.
TABRISI:19:45-48/r14.anchor: وقيل: مليا سويا سليما عن عقوبتي عن ابن عباس وقتادة وعطاء والضحاك

THALABI:v6p216#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p216#2/r6.claim: The father’s question means: Are you turning away from and abandoning worship of my idols?
THALABI:v6p216#2/r6.anchor: أراغب أنت عن آلهتي يا إبراهيم تارك عبادتهم وزاهد فيهم

THALABI:v6p216#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل والكلبي
THALABI:v6p216#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak, Muqatil, and al-Kalbi interpret the threat to stone Abraham as a threat to insult him.

THALABI:v6p216#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p216#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the threat as beating Abraham.

THALABI:v6p216#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p216#2/r9.claim: Another interpretation is that the father threatened to expose Abraham’s situation.

THALABI:v6p216#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r10.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعطاء
THALABI:v6p216#2/r10.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and ʿAta say “leave me for a long while” means leave me safe and unharmed.

THALABI:v6p216#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p216#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as leaving him without blame or reproach.
THALABI:v6p216#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: واعتزلني سالم العرض لا يصيبنك مني معرة

THALABI:v6p216#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r12.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v6p216#2/r12.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the phrase to mean abandoning him for a long time and not speaking to him.
THALABI:v6p216#2/r12.anchor: وقال الكلبي: اتركني واجتنبني طويلا فلا تكلمني

THALABI:v6p216#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v6p216#2/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr explains maliyy as a period of time.

THALABI:v6p216#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p216#2/r14.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
THALABI:v6p216#2/r14.claim: Mujahid and ʿIkrima explain it as “for a while”; the root connotes staying a long time, and al-malawan are night and day.
THALABI:v6p216#2/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعكرمة: حينا، وأصل الحرف المكث، ومنه يقال: تمليت حينا، والملوان الليل والنهار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r1.claim: His father asks whether Abraham is deliberately turning away from his gods; رغب عن means intentionally leaving something. Ending means refrain from the forbidden act, here abusing and insulting them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r1.anchor: رغب عن الشيء إذا تركه عمدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل والسدي والكلبي ومجاهد وابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r2.claim: They interpret I will stone you as I will insult you with vile speech; al-Zajjaj prefers this usage of throwing or stoning someone as a euphemism for cursing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r2.anchor: الضحاك، ومقاتل، والسدي، والكلبي، ومجاهد، وابن جريج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r3.claim: He interprets the threat as I will kill you.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p255#2/r4.claim: He takes it literally as throwing stones until Abraham goes away; another report from Ibn Abbas says he would strike him with stones.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r1.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r1.claim: He gives distinct usages for hajar: a man may move far away, while in fasting the related word refers to a kind of abstention.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r1.anchor: هجر الرجل هجرا إذا تباعد ونأى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r2.claim: He interprets abandon me as keep away from me; al-Kalbi says leave me.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r3.claim: He takes مَلِيّا to mean for a while, as does Mujahid; Ikrima says a long duration, as do Hasan and al-Kalbi, while al-Suddi says forever.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r3.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (يريد حينا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r4.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r4.claim: The adjective maliya denotes a long stretch of time.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r5.claim: He lists dialectal forms for a long period, all derived from length; related words for delaying and extending time occur in the Quran and Arabic poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r5.anchor: الفراء: (يقال: ملوة من الدهر، وملوة، وملوة، وملاوة، وملاوة وكله من الطول)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r6.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r6.claim: He explains it as an ample span of time, an adjective used as a noun, and discusses its morphology through the dropping of a radical in diminutive form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r6.anchor: أبو علي الفارسي: (قالوا انتظرته مليا من الدهر، أي: متسعا منه، وهو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r7.speaker: ابن عباس، رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r7.claim: An alternative interpretation says sound in character and unharmed by me, also reported from Qatada, Atiyya, and al-Dahhak.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r7.anchor: سالم العرض لا يصيبك مني مكروه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r8.claim: He prefers the first temporal meaning, since a person ample or capable in a matter is originally spelled with hamzah; no reader transmitted the hamzated form here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p256/r8.anchor: فلان ملئ بهذا الأمر. والقول هو الأول؛ لأن الملي بالأمر أصله الهمز

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:44-46/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:44-46/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:44-46/r3.claim: His father asks if Abraham is abandoning his idols and threatens to stone or insult him if he does not stop criticizing them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:44-46/r3.anchor: قال } أبوه مجيبا له: { أراغب أنت عن آلهتي } أزاهد فيها وتارك لعبادتها؟! { لئن لم تنته } لئن لم ترجع عن مقالتك في عيبها { لأرجمنك } لأشتمنك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:44-46/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:44-46/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:44-46/r4.claim: The father orders Abraham to leave him for a long time.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:44-46/r4.anchor: واهجرني مليا } زمانا طويلا من الدهر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r1.claim: Abraham's father asks whether he rejects his gods by refusing to worship them.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r2.claim: The threat to stone Abraham means to kill him with stones if he stops insulting and denouncing the idols.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r3.claim: Al-Suddī instead explains the threat of stoning as a threat to insult Abraham.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r4.claim: Qatāda glosses 'leave me for a while' as leave me safe.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r4.anchor: نا يحيى قال: نا سعيد، عن قتادة قال: واهجرني سالما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r5.claim: Mujāhid interprets the requested separation as lasting for a time.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r5.anchor: نا يحيى، قال: نا عاصم بن حكيم أن مجاهدا قال: واهجرني حينا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r6.claim: Al-Hasan, in a report from Qatāda, takes the separation to be for a long time.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r6.anchor: نا يحيى قال: نا سعيد، عن قتادة، عن الحسن قال: واهجرني طويلا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r7.speaker: يحيى
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p227/r7.claim: Yaḥyā summarizes the meaning as prolonging Abraham's estrangement.

SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r1.claim: أراغب أنت has two parses: راغب as a question-supported subject with أنت filling the predicate’s place, or as fronted predicate with أنت as delayed subject.
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أراغب أنت }: يجوز فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أن يكون " راغب " مبتدأ لاعتماده على همزة الاستفهام،

SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r2.claim: The author prefers the first parse because it preserves word order and avoids separating راغب from its complement عن آلهتي with an unrelated أنت.
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r2.anchor: ورجح الأول بوجهين، أحدهما: أنه ليس فيه تقديم ولا تأخير؛

SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r3.claim: مليا may be a temporal accusative meaning ‘for a long time’; ملاوة is used for a long span, as witnessed by a cited line.
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r3.anchor: قوله: " مليا " في نصبه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنه منصوب على الظرف الزماني، أي: زمنا طويلا، ومنه " الملوان " لليل والنهار،

SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r4.speaker: السدي، مهلهل
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r4.claim: Al-Suddi cites a line by Muhalhil as evidence for مليا meaning a long duration.

SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r5.claim: Ibn ‘Abbas interprets مليا as a circumstantial accusative meaning safe and sound.
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r5.anchor: والثاني: أنه منصوب على الحال معناه: سالما سويا. كذا فسره ابن عباس:

SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r6.claim: Ibn ‘Atiyya explains مليا as self-sufficient or independent, from the expression ملي بكذا.
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r6.anchor: وكذلك فسره ابن عطية قال: " معناه: مستبدا، أي: غنيا من قولهم هو ملي بكذا وكذا ".

SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses مليا as capable or able.

SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r8.claim: A third parse makes مليا an adjective of an omitted verbal noun: a broad, prolonged abandonment, like an extended stretch of time.
SAMIN-DURR:19:46/r8.anchor: والثالث: أنه نعت لمصدر محذوف، أي: هجرا مليا يعني: واسعا متطاولا

ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r5.claim: لأرجمنك can mean “I will insult you”; يرمي or يرجم someone can mean insulting him, as in the accusation expressed by يرمون المحصنات.
ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r5.anchor: يقال: فلان يرمي فلانا ويرجم فلانا معناه يشتمه.

ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r6.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r6.claim: Although لأرجمنك could mean stoning Abraham to death, the reported interpretation is that his father threatens to insult him.
ZAJJAJ:v3p332/r6.anchor: وجائز أن يكون (لأرجمنك) لأقتلنك رجما، والذي عليه التفسير أن الرجم ههنا الشتم.

QIRAAT-ER:19:46:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:46:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:46:7#1/r1.claim: The majority's standard form Ibrāhīmu has long ī in the third syllable.
QIRAAT-ER:19:46:7#1/r1.anchor: Standard form: long ī in third syllable (Ibrā-hī-mu); canonical reading of the majority

QIRAAT-ER:19:46:7#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:46:7#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:46:7#2/r1.claim: The canonical variant lengthens the third-syllable vowel to ā rather than ī, reflecting variation in transmission of the name.
QIRAAT-ER:19:46:7#2/r1.anchor: Variant: long ā in third syllable (Ibrā-hā-mu) instead of ī; both canonical (7-readings)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p8#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p8#3/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p8#3/r1.claim: Al-Hasan glosses maliyyan as a long period of time.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p8#3/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ واهجرني مليا ﴾ قال زمانا طويلا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p8#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p8#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p8#3/r2.claim: Qatada glosses maliyyan as safely or unharmed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p8#3/r2.anchor: قال قتادة ﴿ واهجرني مليا ﴾ قال سالما

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r5.claim: One explanation is that Satan is rajim because God has cursed him; rajm can mean cursing, as in the command expelling Satan and Abraham's father's threat.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r5.anchor: أن كونه مرجوما كونه ملعونا من قبل الله تعالى

BAQILLANI:v1p107/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r1.claim: The varieties of badiʿ are numerous, so Bāqillānī gives selected examples rather than an exhaustive catalogue.
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r1.anchor: ووجوه البديع كثيرة جدا فاقتصرنا على ذكر بعضها

BAQILLANI:v1p107/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r2.claim: He rejects the claim that these ornamental devices prove Qurʾānic inimitability: once identified, they can be learned and deliberately practiced, like poetic composition.
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r2.anchor: وليس كذلك عندنا لأن هذه الوجوه إذا وقع التنبيه عليها أمكن التوصل إليها بالتدريب والتعود والتصنع لها

BAQILLANI:v1p107/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r3.claim: The heavily ornamented lāmiyya of Abū Tammām shows that poets can deliberately fill a poem with crafted rhetorical devices.
BAQILLANI:v1p107/r3.anchor: حتى حشي جميع شعره منها واجتهد أن لا يفوته بيت إلا وهو يملؤه من الصنعة كما صنع أبو تمام في لاميته

BURHAN:v3p235/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p235/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p235/r9.claim: Fronting a predicate is also included among devices for assigning focus; the author cites Abraham’s father’s question and the claim about the people’s fortresses.
BURHAN:v3p235/r9.anchor: والخبر كقوله ﴿ قال أراغب أنت عن آلهتي ﴾ 5 وقوله ﴿ وظنوا أنهم مانعتهم حصونهم من الله ﴾ 6

BURHAN:v3p275/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p275/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p275/r4.claim: Fronting راغب in أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ intensifies Abraham’s father’s denial; asking أأنت راغب عنها would not convey the same added disapproval.
BURHAN:v3p275/r4.anchor: ما أفادت زيادة الإنكار على إبراهيم

BURHAN:v1p106/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p106/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p106/r6.claim: Forms of رجم generally mean killing, but Abraham’s father’s threat لأرجمنك means “I will insult you.”
BURHAN:v1p106/r6.anchor: وكل شىء فى القرآن يرجمنكم و يرجموكم فهو القتل

BURHAN:v3p46/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p46/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p46/r1.claim: Oath and condition may govern one another: whichever comes first supplies the answer, and the later element’s answer is omitted or subsumed.
BURHAN:v3p46/r1.anchor: القسم والشرط يدخل كل منهما على الآخر فإن تقدم القسم ودخل الشرط

BURHAN:v3p46/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p46/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p46/r2.claim: In لئن لم تنته لأرجمنك, the first lām introduces the conditional clause and signals an expected oath answer; the lām in لأرجمنك marks that answer.
BURHAN:v3p46/r2.anchor: تقديره والله لئن لم تنته فاللام الداخلة على الشرط ليس بلام القسم

ITQAN:v2p417/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p417/r13.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p417/r13.claim: Ibn Faris says rajm generally means killing, but la-arjumannaka means I will insult you and rajman bil-ghayb means conjecture.
ITQAN:v2p417/r13.anchor: وكل ما فيه من الرجم فهو القتل إلا ﴿ لأرجمنك ﴾ فمعناه لأشتمنك و ﴿ رجما بالغيب ﴾ أي ظنا

ITQAN:v2p319/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p319/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p319/r5.claim: Wahjurni means leave me or keep away from me.

DAMGHANI:v1p196/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r6.claim: Rajm can mean insulting or cursing someone verbally.
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r6.anchor: الرجم الشتم قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r1.claim: Rajm originally means forcefully throwing a stone; it extends to slander or abuse, and can mean stones themselves, uncertain conjecture, or defending one’s people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r1.anchor: الرجم في الأصل : إلقاء الحجر بشدة الدفع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r2.claim: The hadith phrase lā tarjumu qabrī means leave my grave level and do not pile stones on it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r2.anchor: لا ترجموا قبري ) ، أي : دعوه مستويا لا تدعوا عليه حجارة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r6.claim: A fourth sense is insult or verbal abuse, as Abraham’s father threatens him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الرجم في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r3.claim: Rajm can mean insult: abuse is verbal throwing, as is also reflected in the root meaning of qadhf.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r3.anchor: وأصل القذف: الرمي، ومنه قول أبي إبراهيم له: لأرجمنك

NASHR:v2p221/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p221/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p221/r2.claim: The source counts 33 occurrences of Ibrāhīm, including 15 in al-Baqara and further instances across the listed sūras, including Maryam’s vocative in 19:46.

NASHR:v2p221/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p221/r3.speaker: هشام
NASHR:v2p221/r3.claim: Hishām reads Ibrāhīm as Ibrāhām, with an alif, at all 33 occurrences.
NASHR:v2p221/r3.anchor: فروى هشام من جميع طرقه إبراهام بألف في المواضع المذكورة

NASHR:v2p221/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p221/r4.speaker: ابن ذكوان
NASHR:v2p221/r4.claim: Ibn Dhakwān’s routes differ: al-Nuqāsh from al-Akhfash and al-Muṭawwiʿī from al-Ṣūrī read the usual yāʾ form, while al-Ramlī from al-Ṣūrī reads with alif; most other Iraqi al-Akhfash routes also use alif.
NASHR:v2p221/r4.anchor: واختلف عن ابن ذكوان، فروى النقاش عن الأخفش عنه بالياء كالجماعة

NASHR:v2p221/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p221/r5.speaker: المغاربة، بعض المشارقة عن ابن الأخرم عن الأخفش
NASHR:v2p221/r5.claim: A further Ibn Dhakwān report uses alif in al-Baqara only and yāʾ elsewhere; this is the common Maghribī transmission and one eastern route, and al-Mahdawī records only this form.
NASHR:v2p221/r5.anchor: وفصل بعضهم عنه، فروى الألف في البقرة خاصة والياء في غيرها، وهي رواية المغاربة قاطبة وبعض المشارقة عن ابن الأخرم عن الأخفش

SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.claim: With a demonstrative, the following noun is the predicate and an accusative descriptor is a circumstantial state, as in هذا عبد الله منطلقا.
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.anchor: الأسماء المبهمة فقولك هذا عبد الله منطلقا وهؤلاء قومك منطلقين

SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.claim: This construction draws attention to someone in a state such as departing; it does not identify an otherwise unknown person as Abdullah.
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.anchor: والمعنى أنك تريد أن تنبهه له منطلقا

SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.claim: The demonstratives share this construction: ذاك points to something distant, while أولئك and the other forms follow the same pattern.
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.anchor: إلا أنك إذا قلت ذاك فأنت تنبهه لشئ متراخ

SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.claim: With هو and related pronouns, the accusative state should clarify or confirm the referent, as معروفا or بينا; an action like منطلقا does not identify him.

SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.speaker: ابن دارة
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.claim: Ibn Dāra's line illustrates the pronoun construction with معروفا as an identifying circumstantial state.
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.anchor: قال ابن دارة # % أنا ابن دارة معروفا بها نسبي

SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.claim: A demonstrative may also identify something present, as in هذا عبد الله فاعرفه, but here it serves recognition rather than marking a pronoun.
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.anchor: ليس علامة للمضمر ولكنك أردت أن تعرف شيئا بحضرتك

SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.claim: Pronouns can be followed by circumstantial descriptions in boasting or threatening contexts, when the speaker reminds the listener of known qualities such as generosity or bravery.
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.anchor: وأنا عبد الله فاخرا أو موعدا

SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.claim: A pronoun normally assumes an already known referent, so a following name or action as mere new information is unsuitable; an unknown speaker behind a wall can identify himself, and an ordinary noun such as أخوك permits the construction.
SIBAWAYH:والأسماءالمبهمةهذاوهذانوهذهوهات.anchor: أراد أن يخبرك بالانطلاق ولم يقل هو ولا أنا
